proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: An androgen receptor pathway inhibitor can act on hormone production or on the receptor itself. These are different interventions. Testosterone and dihydrotestosterone are androgen hormones; the full-length androgen receptor is a hormone-responsive transcription factor that helps regulate which DNA instructions are read into RNA. Bicalutamide and enzalutamide act at its ligand-binding region rather than removing the hormone supply. Blocking this receptor is also different from blocking the estrogen receptor. A receptor can be present while its partners, sequence, abundance or cellular setting change what an antagonist does.
proofPassages.explanation: NCI prostate hormone therapy distinguishes production reduction from receptor competition;this mechanism does not transfer prostate efficacy to breast cancer.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Full-length AR has distinct regions for transcriptional regulation, DNA binding and ligand binding. Androgens can change receptor interactions, nuclear localization and regulatory-DNA binding, with effects determined by partners, accessible DNA and receptor form. Tran's antiandrogen experiments in prostate models tested binding, nuclear movement and transcriptional effects separately. An RNA signal does not characterize a truncated protein or transfer those prostate results to breast-cancer treatment.
proofPassages.explanation: Full-length domain and nuclear-route language is compared with human UniProt FUNCTION comments and targeted prostate-model experiments;not a universal localization rule.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Receptor amount, location, transcription and growth dependence are different observations. Nuclear AR immunostaining reports protein in sampled cells; a luminal androgen receptor, or LAR, label is a versioned RNA-classifier result. TBCRC 032 correlative analyses found AR protein expression alone insufficient to identify AR-dependent tumors. Neither staining nor classifier membership alone proves patient benefit.
proofPassages.explanation: New AR-positive TNBC lead corrects the protein-stain/RNA-subtype conflation. The actual TBCRC032 abstract states the insufficiency of AR protein alone. Existing LAR and AR owner wording already separates these measurements.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Some triple-negative breast cancers show androgen receptor protein on a specified staining assay. That finding differs from an RNA subtype and does not by itself establish receptor dependence or benefit from an AR drug.
proofPassages.explanation: New AR-positive TNBC lead corrects the protein-stain/RNA-subtype conflation. The actual TBCRC032 abstract states the insufficiency of AR protein alone. Existing LAR and AR owner wording already separates these measurements.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Follow the signal through four locations: hormone supply, receptor binding inside a cell, nuclear regulation of DNA-to-RNA transcription and a receptor form with a missing binding region. Splicing assembles RNA from selected segments, so different messages can encode different receptor proteins. TBCRC 032 identified AR-V7 and AR-V12 transcripts lacking the ligand-binding domain in a small patient analysis. A drug aimed at that region and an intervention that lowers hormone supply therefore test different steps. Neither a receptor drawing nor a positive stain establishes growth dependence or benefit in breast cancer.
proofPassages.explanation: Hu targeted paragraphs demonstrate specified AR-V7 forms and transfected prostate systems. The cartoon is not a claim about every splice form or breast response.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Traina and colleagues studied enzalutamide in a single-arm phase II trial of locally advanced or metastatic androgen-receptor-positive triple-negative breast cancer. The breast-optimised immunohistochemistry assay allowed enrolment with more than 0% nuclear staining. The evaluable subgroup additionally required at least 10% nuclear staining and a postbaseline assessment: 78 of 118 enrolled patients met that definition. The abstract reported clinical benefit at 16 weeks in 25% of all enrolled patients and 33% of that subgroup. The trial registry defines this endpoint as complete or partial response, or stable disease for at least 16 weeks. It is not the percentage with tumour shrinkage, and a single treatment arm does not measure a survival advantage over another treatment.
proofPassages.explanation: The complete registry primary-outcome objects include CR,PR or qualifying SD;one-third CBR is not one-third shrinkage or a randomized survival estimate.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: If a fictional report says a receptor-positive group had a 16-week clinical benefit rate of one third, first inspect the endpoint definition and analysis population. When qualifying stable disease is included, one third does not mean one third of tumours shrank. Ask which assay defined positivity, who enrolled, who entered the evaluable denominator and how long disease control had to last. The receptor supplies a mechanism hypothesis; expression supplies an assay result; benefit needs evidence for the particular drug, population and outcome.
proofPassages.explanation: The complete registry primary-outcome objects include CR,PR or qualifying SD;one-third CBR is not one-third shrinkage or a randomized survival estimate.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: CDK4 and CDK6 help phosphorylate retinoblastoma protein, or RB, near the G1-to-S transition toward DNA copying. Their usual arrest mechanism depends on a functional RB restraint on cell-cycle transcription; detecting RB protein alone does not establish an intact circuit, and loss of RB1 can remove that route. CDK2 works with cyclins E and A in progression around DNA replication. These are selected overlapping roles, not exclusive assignments for every cell state. Cyclin E abundance by itself does not select a particular CDK2 inhibitor.
proofPassages.explanation: A conditional functional-RB mechanism is retained;the NCI short definition does not validate a patient selection assay.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: CDK7 contributes to transcription initiation and also activates other CDKs. These jobs cannot be sealed into separate boxes. If a test reports a fall in a short-lived transcript after a transcription-directed intervention, that is an RNA-output observation to verify, not proof of the cell-cycle arrest associated with CDK4/6 inhibition. The exact transcript and its response need to be measured.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Selectivity depends on the compound and achieved exposure; one drug can inhibit several CDKs. Horiuchi and colleagues tested purvalanol A and dinaciclib in breast-cancer models with elevated MYC, and used individual kinase knockdown to investigate attribution. Their paper describes dinaciclib activity against CDK1, CDK2, CDK5 and CDK9 and reports cell-death effects after CDK1 depletion in the tested triple-negative lines. This preclinical result is not a rule for choosing a modern CDK4/6 or CDK2 drug from MYC expression. Engagement, cell-cycle change and cell death remain different observations.
proofPassages.explanation: Compound,selectivity and exposure are needed. Dictionary potential-activity language does not supply efficacy or inevitable apoptosis.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional culture that stops dividing during drug exposure and regrows after washout, the observed pattern supports reversible arrest. It does not establish selective killing or durable tumour control. Test attribution to the intended kinase, measure death and longer-term regrowth, and compare relevant control cells. A pause used to protect marrow and an intervention intended to control a tumour can involve related machinery while pursuing different outcomes.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. proofPassages.supportingExcerpt: A kinase transfers a phosphate group to a substrate; phosphorylation does not always turn that substrate on. A simplified p53/G1 and WEE1/G2 checkpoint drawing can motivate a hypothesis after defined functional checkpoint loss; a TP53 sequence variant alone does not prove that the first pause is absent or that a second pause is a validated treatment dependency. proofPassages.explanation: WEE1 supplies an inhibitory CDK1 phosphate. The p53/DNA-damage rationale is not a universal TP53 rule.
